Proceedings in this case have arisen from filing of DAR in FIR No.443/2019 of PS Seemapuri,

As per the facts, on 14.07.2019 at about 08.00 a.m. MACT No.294/2020 SHELENDER SHELENDER MALIK Page 1 MALIK Date: 2024.10.03 16:15:12 +0530 petitioner/injured was going to take bus for Gandhi Nagar for attending her duty, in the meanwhile offending bus bearing registration no.DL-1PC-5514 being driven by its driver at very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came from back side and hit the petitioner with great force due to which petitioner fell down and bus ran over her.
It is stated that driver stopped the bus after shouting by people and petitioner was pulled out from under the bus.
After some time police came and removed the petitioner to GTB Hospital.
Upon completion of investigation DAR was filed before the Tribunal.

My issues wise findings are as under :
Issue No.1 12.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.

14. Though petitioner/injured (PW1) was cross examined, however nothing substantive came in her cross examination to disbelieve the version given by her.
During cross examination PW1 stated that she was on way to Gandhi Nagar on the date of accident and she saw the bus before it came to her as the bus was around some distance from her.
PW1 denied that accident occurred due to her negligence and that it was not caused by respondent no.1.

Even otherwise evidence of petitioner has been corroborated from the documents annexed with DAR Ex.PW1/2 (colly.) including FIR,
statement/complaint of petitioner/injured, MLC of petitioner, site plan, mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, seizure memo of offending bus etc.

15. Respondent no.2 has examined one witness R2W1 Dharminder Kala who deposed by way of affidavit that he is authorized representative of respondent no.2 company which is the owner of offending bus no.DL-1PC-5514.
R2W1 says that respondent no.2 company operates a fleet of cluster buses in Delhi in pursuance of concession agreement executed between R2 and Department of Transport, Govt. of NCT of Delhi.

Witness says that the offending vehicle has not caused the accident as alleged which was driven by respondent no.1, rather petitioner met with the accident due to her own fault.

R2W1 says that petitioner was casually and negligently walking o the road on the day of accident, due to her fault fell down on the road and sustained injuries and she has not met with the accident with the vehicle in question.
Witness says that FIR is after though and police without proper investigation registered the FIR.

Witness also says that vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3 vide policy Ex.R2W1/2, its certificate is Ex.R2W1/3, permit and RC is Ex.R2W1/4 and Ex.R2W1/5.
16.
During cross examination witness R2W1 says that police called him at the police station Seemapuri on the day of accident and bus was lying at police station.
Witness also says that the bus driver was in custody of police at police station.
Apart from oral evidence of R2W1, there is nothing in the testimony of this witness to disregard the evidence of petitioner/injured and the police case documents placed on record.

It is also matter of record that the respondent no.1/driver of the offending bus has not entered into the witness box to rebut the allegations that he caused the accident in which petitioner sustained injuries.
Even otherwise report u/s 173 Cr.PC filed by the police shows that respondent no.1/driver has been charge sheeted for causing accident in question.

Mere assertion that police registered the FIR without proper investigation, in the absence of any evidence to the same, is not sufficient to discard the evidence of PW1 and police report filed before the criminal court.
17. As discussed above, there is sufficient evidence to conclude that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no.DL-1PC-5514.
Issue accordingly MACT No.294/2020

4 "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.
So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned

,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
19. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, MACT No.294/2020 SHELENDER MALIK Date:
2024.10.03 16:15:59 +0530 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
Dar - Priya vs Vinod Kumar on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191756366/
5

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
MACT No.294/2020 Digitally signed Page 8  by SHELENDER  SHELENDER MALIK  MALIK Date: 2024.10.03  16:16:05 +0530

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
20.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses 21.
Petitioner/injured (PW1) in her evidence has stated that she was initially taken to GTB Hospital where she remained hospitalized for about one month.
Petitioner stated that after discharge she remained on bed rest for around three to four months.
Witness also says that she spent huge sum of money on medicines, treatment etc.
However it is matter of record that no medical bills have been placed on record by the petitioner.

But fact remains that as per MLC of petitioner she suffered injuries on injuries on her right foot dorsal aspect, deformity of left lower limb, restricted movement of right lower limb, tenderness of back and left shoulder joint and the injuries suffered by the petitioner have been opined to be grievous in nature.

Therefore keeping in view the evidence of Dar - Priya vs Vinod Kumar on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191756366/
6 petitioner as well as nature of injuries, this Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.10,000/- as a lump sum amount under the head of medical expenses on estimate basis.
Loss of earning during treatment 22.
Petitioner in her evidence deposed that at the time of accident she was working as daily wages worker in the garment shop/factory MACT No.294/2020 by SHELENDER Page 9 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK

Date:
2024.10.03 16:16:12 +0530 wherein she was earning Rs.350/- to Rs.400/- daily and she remained on bed for more than one year due to accidental injuries.
However during cross examination petitioner admitted that she has not placed on record any document of her work but she got remuneration when she went to work.

In the absence of same, notional income of the petitioner is taken at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi at the time of accident as the accident has taken place in Delhi and DAR has been filed by the police of PS Seemapuri, Delhli, which is Rs.14,468/- per month.
23. Petitioner/injured (PW1) in her affidavit deposed that in the accident she received serious/grievous injuries all over her body and she was taken to GTB Hospital from the place of accident.
Petitioner deposed that due to accident her collarbone was broken and both her legs were broken, an iron rod was fitted in her left leg.
Witness says that she was treated in hospital and remained hospitalized for about more than a month and after her discharge she remained on bed for more than a year.

However during cross examination petitioner admitted that she has not placed any document pertaining to treatment after the accident neither she has placed any medical bills and doctor's prescription.

However perusal of MLC of injured/ petitioner shows that she received abrasion on right foot dorsal aspect, deformity of left lower limb, restricted movement of right lower limb, tenderness of back and left shoulder joint.
As such taking into consideration MLC of petitioner and her evidence, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner must have remained confined to bed and took treatment for period of two months.
Therefore petitioner is entitled for loss of income for sum of Rs.28,936/- (Rs.14,468/- X 02 months).
Loss of future earning due to disability 24.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC MACT No.294/2020 Digitally signed Page 10 SHELENDER by SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.03 16:16:18 +0530 343,
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

sentences.text: However in the present case there is no disability certificate of the petitioner on record.
It is matter of record that vide order dated 27.10.2023 upon moving an application, petitioner was referred to medical board of GTB Hospital for assessing her permanent disability.
However no disability certificate has been received or filed in this Tribunal.

Even otherwise on 01.10.2024 petitioner herself appeared in the court and gave the statement to the effect that claim petition may be disposed off on merits as per the available evidence on judicial record as there is likelihood of delay in receiving of disability certificate and she does not want to rely on disability certificate.

7 reach to the conclusion of sustaining any permanent disability.
Thus, in view of this position of the matter, this Tribunal does not find it a fit case for awarding compensation to the petitioner under this head.

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
25.

Though petitioner in her evidence has claimed that she spent huge sum of money on medicines,
treatment, special diet etc. however she has not filed any documentary proof in support of the same.
Even no quantifiable amount has been given by the petitioner which she alleged to have spent on special diet and conveyance charges.

Taking the evidence and the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner in the accident, this Tribunal finds that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- each for special diet and conveyance charges.
MACT No.294/2020 SHELENDER  Page 11
MALIK Date: 2024.10.03  16:16:24 +0530  Attendant Charges 26.
On the question of attendant charges, petitioner in her deposition has not claimed any amount for attendant charges.

However as per the evidence of petitioner and the MLC placed on record she suffered injuries on her right foot dorsal aspect, deformity of left lower limb, restricted movement of right lower limb, tenderness of back and left shoulder joint.
Thus it would be fitness of things to grant petitioner attendant charges at parity with minimum wages of an unskilled worker in Delhi for a period of two months, which is Rs.14,468/- per month.

Therefore this Tribunal is considered view that petitioner is certainly entitled for compensation for attendant charges of Rs.28,936/-
(Rs.14,468/- X 02 months).
NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings 27.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12.
On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:

8 (a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
28.

In this case, as per the MLC of the petitioner, she was found to have suffered injuries on her right foot dorsal aspect, deformity of left MACT No.294/2020 SHELENDER by SHELENDER Page 12 MALIK Date: 2024.10.03 16:16:29 +0530 lower limb, restricted movement of right lower limb,
tenderness of back and left shoulder joint.

Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered pain and suffering during her treatment and therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of Rs.25,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
Loss of Amenities 29.

Having considered the evidence of PW1 and the MLC of the petitioner wherein doctor opined the nature of injuries suffered by her to be grievous, this Tribunal of the considered view that petitioner must have lost amenities of life on account of injuries suffered in the accident.
Therefore taking into consideration nature of injuries, disability, he is awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.

However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.
(MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
Mere assertion that police registered the FIR without proper investigation, in the absence of any evidence to the same, is not sufficient to discard the evidence of PW1 and police report filed before the criminal court.
17. As discussed above, there is sufficient evidence to conclude that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no.DL-1PC-5514.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. 1995 AIR 755.
19. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
